slides.0.title: Regulatory Evolution and Diploma Arguments
slides.0.subtitle: The VQA histories of Ontario and BC, new GIs and essay structure
slides.1.title: Ontario's regulatory path
slides.1.highlights.0.title: From voluntary to law
slides.1.highlights.0.content: VQA began voluntary in 1988, was incorporated into regulation in 1998, and the 1999 Vintners Quality Alliance Act was proclaimed on 29 June 2000, creating the Ontario Wine Appellation Authority to oversee it (Wine With Seth, Fine Vintage)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Areas added step by step
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Niagara Peninsula and Lake Erie North Shore came early, Prince Edward County joined in 2007, and the South Islands sub-appellation was added in July 2015. Each step shows the system expanding as the industry matured
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Essay angle
slides.1.highlights.2.content: One can argue that VQA prioritises authenticity of origin over a quality guarantee: it regulates origin, variety and labelling but not flavour, and "Cellared in Canada" once confused consumers
slides.1.content: Be ready to narrate the system as a timeline.
slides.2.title: BC's regulatory path
slides.2.highlights.0.title: VQA to the BCWA
slides.2.highlights.0.content: BC VQA began in 1990; Reg 79/2005 applied from 1 August 2005 with the BC Wine Authority (BCWA); from 27 July 2018 Reg 168/2018 replaced Reg 79/2005 and has been amended through 2025 (BC Laws)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The four new GIs of 2018
slides.2.highlights.1.content: On 12 April 2018 four new GIs were announced — Thompson Valley, Shuswap, Lillooet and Kootenays (previously six including BC itself, with Golden Mile Bench as the sole sub-GI), following the 2016 BC Wine Appellation Task Group; "Wines of Distinction" became "British Columbia wine"
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The BCWA's role
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Wineries making 100% BC wine must join the BCWA (over 200 wineries, about 90% of licensed grape wineries and over 95% of BC wine). The current GI threshold is 85% from that GI; earlier thresholds are reported inconsistently and are not tested
slides.2.content: BC's rules were revised repeatedly; always cite the year.
slides.3.title: Structuring Diploma essays
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Common essay themes
slides.3.highlights.0.content: "Is Canada's climate an advantage or a weakness?", "Does VQA protect consumers?" and "Should icewine remain the flagship?" all suit a two-sided structure backed by evidence
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Evidence checklist
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Climate: the January 2024 freeze and wildfire smoke; institutions: Ontario's 2000 VQA Act, BC's 2018 new GIs and the end of Cellared in Canada; market: about 30% domestic share, icewine-led exports; styles: Tidal Bay, Vin du Québec PGI, skin-fermented whites and Appassimento
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Mistakes to avoid
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Do not treat advocacy figures as settled; do not mix up Reg 79/2005 and Reg 168/2018; do not say all icewine comes from Ontario (over 90% does, but every region makes some); do not claim Canada is shielded from climate change
slides.3.content: A good essay is claim, evidence and limits.
When was Ontario's Vintners Quality Alliance Act proclaimed?
Which regulation did BC's Reg 168/2018 replace?
Which is NOT one of the four GIs announced in April 2018?
What is BC's current minimum for a GI claim?
"Wines of Distinction" was renamed in 2018 to?
What is the best approach in a Diploma essay?
A. Claim, evidence and limits, citing source and year
C. Treat advocacy figures as settled
Good essays state claim, evidence and limits.
